headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: slim can expose sensitive container artifacts while transformers can ingest and act on them without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: slim reads and writes filesystem artifacts and emits stdin/stdout, while transformers can read files and process model inputs. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content in slim’s artifacts influence transformers. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF slim outputs attacker-controlled text into a shared file that transformers later reads
IF the operator copies slim stdout into a transformers prompt or pipeline input
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Treat slim outputs as untrusted data
Add a manual review step before transformers consumes slim artifacts
Use file allowlists for inputs to transformers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, and has broad network egress. transformers also has broad egress and reads/writes files. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive container data can be exposed or uploaded without strong isolation. The pairwise path is plausible from profiles alone, so severity is high.
conditions: IF slim writes certificate files, env vars, or registry credentials into a directory transformers can read
IF transformers sends shared files or prompts containing slim artifacts to a remote backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Rotate any registry credentials used by slim
Disable network egress for transformers during shared-file processing
Review and delete exported artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read and write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and slim also executes shell commands. Without locking or isolated directories, concurrent writes to the same workspace can overwrite artifacts or corrupt outputs. The profiles show overlapping mutable access, so conflict risk is high even though git state is not involved.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF the operator runs them concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Use OS-level file locks
Make outputs append-only where possible
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-managed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim produces container and vulnerability artifacts, and transformers can consume files and generate downstream text or pipeline outputs. If transformers treats slim’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect reports or actions. There is no documented verification boundary, but no direct action authority is shown, so medium fits.
conditions: IF transformers consumes slim-generated reports without validation
IF downstream automation trusts transformers output derived from slim artifacts
mitigations: Require human review of slim-derived outputs
Add schema validation before transformers ingests reports
Cross-check critical findings against source artifacts
Log provenance for each transformed file
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, environment variables, and vulnerability data, while transformers handles general multimodal content and broad file I/O. If regulated secrets or sensitive infrastructure data flow into transformers, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not show certifications or residency guarantees, so the safest supported rating is medium.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or vulnerability data from slim are stored in transformers-managed files
IF the deployment requires retention or residency controls not enforced by both agents
mitigations: Classify and segregate sensitive inputs
Delete temporary files after processing
Confirm retention settings for both agents
Avoid placing secrets in transformer inputs
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
